source: JSON text exchanged between systems that are not part of a closed ecosystem MUST be encoded using UTF-8

selectedIdea.title: Why an interoperable format still needs an encoding rule
selectedIdea.description: Why an interoperable format still needs an encoding rule
selectedIdea.rationale: Why an interoperable format still needs an encoding rule
selectedIdea.evidence: JSON text exchanged between systems that are not part of a closed ecosystem MUST be encoded using UTF-8

narrative:
### Selected Story
The story is about JSON text exchanged between systems outside a closed ecosystem and the encoding rule that applies to that exchange. The key point is that using an interoperable format does not leave the text’s encoding unspecified: the required encoding is UTF-8.

### Story Progression
- **Context:** Introduce JSON as a format whose text can be exchanged between systems.
- **Development:** Establish the specific rule: JSON text exchanged between systems that are not part of a closed ecosystem must use UTF-8 encoding.
- **Endpoint:** Clarify that the encoding rule is part of the requirements for this kind of JSON exchange.

### Critical Constraints
- Do not invent a reason for the UTF-8 requirement or claim benefits beyond the stated encoding rule.

source: Ice is less dense than liquid water which is why your ice cubes float in your glass.

selectedIdea.title: Why solid water floats
selectedIdea.evidence: Ice is less dense than liquid water which is why your ice cubes float in your glass.

narrative:
### Selected Story
Explain why ice floats in liquid water: ice is less dense than liquid water, a difference that accounts for the familiar sight of ice cubes floating in a glass. The reader should understand that the explanation rests on the relationship between the density of solid water and liquid water.

### Story Progression
- **Context:** Begin with the familiar observation of ice cubes floating in a glass of water.
- **Development:** Establish the relevant comparison: ice is less dense than liquid water.
- **Endpoint:** Connect that difference in density to the central idea that solid water floats in liquid water.

source: Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) is based on International Atomic Time (TAI), but it is adjusted by leap seconds

selectedIdea.title: Why atomic time and civil time diverge
selectedIdea.description: Why atomic time and civil time diverge
selectedIdea.rationale: Why atomic time and civil time diverge
selectedIdea.evidence: Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) is based on International Atomic Time (TAI), but it is adjusted by leap seconds

narrative:
### Selected Story
The story explains the relationship between International Atomic Time (TAI) and Coordinated Universal Time (UTC): UTC is based on TAI, but leap-second adjustments distinguish the two. The reader should understand that UTC is not simply identical to TAI; the supplied material establishes their relationship and the adjustments, but not why those adjustments are made.

### Story Progression
- **Context:** Introduce TAI and UTC as the two time standards at the center of the story.
- **Development:** Explain their supported relationship: UTC is based on TAI and is adjusted by leap seconds.
- **Endpoint:** Clarify that UTC’s basis in TAI does not make the two identical; the stated distinction is the leap-second adjustments.

### Critical Constraints
- Do not explain why leap seconds are used or make broader claims about how the two standards diverge; the inputs establish only that UTC is based on TAI and adjusted by leap seconds.

narrative:
### Selected Story
The story explains what the standard $250,000 FDIC deposit insurance amount is measured against: coverage is specified per depositor, per FDIC-insured bank, and per ownership category. The reader should understand that these three dimensions define the basis of the standard coverage figure.

### Story Progression
- **Context:** Introduce the standard deposit insurance amount of $250,000.
- **Development:** Explain that the amount is specified per depositor, per FDIC-insured bank, and per ownership category.
- **Endpoint:** Clarify that these three dimensions define the basis for understanding the standard coverage amount.
